subject: maths
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: Skip counting by 2s, 5s and 10s
outcomes: Learner can count a large collection by making groups of 2, 5 or 10 and skip counting
misconceptions: Loses track when skip counting and counts the last group by ones from 1
hooks: Count shells on the beach in pairs, chappals by 2s

topics.title: Estimating a large collection
outcomes: Learner can estimate how many objects there are and check by grouping
misconceptions: Believes an estimate is wrong unless it is the exact answer
hooks: Guess the number of peanuts in a paper cone

topics.title: Cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere
outcomes: Learner can identify and name common 3D shapes in objects around them
misconceptions: Thinks a cylinder lying down is a different shape from one standing up
hooks: Dice = cube, matchbox = cuboid, gas cylinder, ice-cream cone, ball

topics.title: Flat and curved surfaces
outcomes: Learner can tell whether a shape has flat or curved faces and predict if it will roll, slide or stack
misconceptions: Believes a cone cannot slide because it has a curved surface
hooks: Stack steel tiffin boxes; why can’t you stack balls?

topics.title: Tens and ones up to 100
outcomes: Learner can represent and read two-digit numbers as tens and ones, and 100 as ten tens
misconceptions: Mixes up seventy and seventeen because the number names sound alike
Thinks 100 has to be written as 1000 because "hundred" sounds bigger
hooks: Notes of ₹10 and ₹1 coins to make the price of a toy

topics.title: Comparing and ordering numbers to 100
outcomes: Learner can compare two-digit numbers using place value and arrange them in order
misconceptions: Thinks 39 is greater than 41 because 9 is greater than 1
hooks: Which bus number is bigger, 39 or 41?

topics.title: Patterns in the 100 grid
outcomes: Learner can find and explain patterns of +1, +10, -10 on a hundred grid
misconceptions: Believes moving down one row adds 1
hooks: Find house numbers on a long street

topics.title: From 3D objects to 2D shapes
outcomes: Learner can trace the faces of 3D objects and name the 2D shapes formed (circle, triangle, rectangle, square)
misconceptions: Believes a square turned on its corner becomes a "diamond" and is no longer a square
hooks: Shadow puppets (Togalu Gombeyaata) of Karnataka; trace a bangle and a matchbox

topics.title: Sides and corners of 2D shapes
outcomes: Learner can count sides and corners of simple 2D shapes
misconceptions: Thinks a triangle must always point upwards with equal sides
hooks: Find triangles in the kite you fly on Makar Sankranti

topics.title: Standing, sleeping and slanting lines
outcomes: Learner can draw and identify straight lines in different orientations and curved lines
misconceptions: Thinks a slanting line is not straight
hooks: Find standing and sleeping lines in letters of your name and on the cricket pitch

topics.title: Drawing pictures with lines
outcomes: Learner can make pictures and patterns using straight and curved lines
misconceptions: Believes curved lines cannot be part of a shape
hooks: Draw a kolam using dots and lines

topics.title: Adding two-digit numbers
outcomes: Learner can add two-digit numbers with and without regrouping using tens and ones
misconceptions: Writes 27 + 15 as 312 (adds columns but does not regroup)
Adds tens digit to ones digit (37 + 2 = 57)
hooks: Diyas for Diwali: 27 from didi, 15 from mummy

topics.title: Subtracting two-digit numbers
outcomes: Learner can subtract two-digit numbers with and without regrouping and check by adding
misconceptions: Always subtracts the smaller digit from the larger in each column (52 - 17 = 45)
hooks: 42 balloons for decoration, 18 burst

topics.title: Mental strategies
outcomes: Learner can use jumps of 10 and near-10 numbers to add and subtract in the head
misconceptions: Believes mental maths means you must not use any strategy, only memory
hooks: Add 9 by adding 10 then taking away 1 while buying flowers

topics.title: Why we need a uniform unit
outcomes: Learner can explain why measuring with different hand-spans gives different answers and use a uniform unit
misconceptions: Thinks a bigger number of units always means a longer object, even when units differ
hooks: Measure a dupatta using your hand and dadi’s

topics.title: Comparing weight and capacity
outcomes: Learner can compare weights with a simple balance and capacity by pouring
misconceptions: Believes a taller bottle always holds more water
hooks: Which holds more: a tall thin glass or a wide lota?

topics.title: Equal groups as multiplication
outcomes: Learner can describe equal groups as "3 times 4" and find the total by skip counting
misconceptions: Thinks 3 groups of 4 and 4 groups of 3 give different totals
hooks: Packets of 4 biscuits for 3 friends

topics.title: Sharing equally
outcomes: Learner can share a collection equally and say how many each gets and how many are left
misconceptions: Believes sharing equally means everyone gets "some", not the same number
hooks: Share 12 jalebis among 4 cousins

topics.title: Days, weeks, months and seasons
outcomes: Learner can name days of the week and months in order and use a calendar to find dates
misconceptions: Thinks every month has 30 days
hooks: Find your birthday and Holi on the calendar

topics.title: Seasons through the year
outcomes: Learner can link months to seasons in their region and describe changes
misconceptions: Believes all of India has the same seasons at the same time
hooks: When do mangoes come? when does the monsoon reach your town?

topics.title: Making amounts up to ₹100
outcomes: Learner can make an amount up to ₹100 using different coins and notes
misconceptions: Thinks ₹50 written as one note is less than five ₹10 notes
hooks: Tickets for the giant wheel at the mela

topics.title: Total cost and change
outcomes: Learner can find the total cost of two items and the change returned
misconceptions: Believes the shopkeeper returns change equal to the price
hooks: Buy a ₹35 toy with a ₹50 note

topics.title: Collecting data and tally marks
outcomes: Learner can collect information by asking a question and record it with tally marks
misconceptions: Draws the fifth tally mark as another standing line instead of crossing the four
hooks: Favourite fruit survey in class

topics.title: Reading a simple pictograph
outcomes: Learner can read a pictograph and answer comparison questions
misconceptions: Thinks the row with bigger pictures has more items
hooks: Pictograph of vehicles passing the school gate
